An admin allowed to create users can select and submit a CSV through the application's user-management experience.

verdicts.quote: An otherwise readable CSV omitting a required column is rejected with feedback identifying the missing column.
verdicts.missing: A builder still has to decide how to handle unexpected columns and a file with no header row.

verdicts.missing: The encoding, treatment of a byte-order mark, and accepted record line endings are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: After a file is rejected or an account write fails, the admin finds no accounts created by that submission … that user receives the corresponding communication after a successful import.
A file with exactly 1,000 valid user records can be imported when it satisfies the other requirements. A file with 1,001 otherwise valid user records is refused.

A zero-byte file or a file containing only non-record content allowed by the accepted layout produces feedback that there are no users to import. … One successful CSV submission creates one user per eligible record.
If they resubmit the original CSV or include one account that already exists, the import reports the conflict and the original accounts keep their current details.
If ordinary creation under the same settings sends an invitation or other new-account communication to a user, that user receives the corresponding communication after a successful import.
verdicts.missing: The builder must decide whether to send all invitations together or pace delivery, and at what rate.

verdicts.quote: An imported account enters the same setup state as an equivalent normally created account, including any existing activation or verification requirement. … After a successful import, the recipient follows the deployment's normal account setup process.
Where normal user creation emits an audit record, the operator can find a corresponding creation record for an imported account with the information normally captured for that action.
verdicts.missing: The clause leaves open whether the records identify the importing admin, the import time, and which accounts belonged to that import.

verdicts.quote: After the admin resolves the cause of a prior rejection, they can submit an eligible CSV using the same import entry point.
verdicts.missing: The builder has no rule for admin-initiated cancellation or for selecting only failed rows to retry.

verdicts.quote: Existing callers submitting their usual single-user creation inputs continue to get the same results under the same permissions and settings. … Import leaves existing accounts untouched.
A record containing a value the normal creation path rejects for its format, length, or allowed values is rejected on the same basis.
verdicts.missing: The clause covers overlong fields. A builder still has to decide how to prevent submitted values in spreadsheet-readable results from executing as formulas.
